## 1. spike14a recovered fraction of the R0 -> R1 gap, with paired-bootstrap CI

Definition: (mean L - mean R0) / (mean R1 - mean R0), R0 = C0 (T-adapt3-full), R1 = true theta. The same resampled episodes are used in numerator and denominator. L-dec4 = per-episode mean over its 3 training seeds (the table.md convention); L-ens = `ens_dec4` (mean theta_hat of the 3 models, post hoc). Percentile 95% CI of the ratio; 'den CI' is the 95% CI of the denominator (the R1-R0 gap) so the reader can see how unstable the ratio is.

## 2. Equivalence table (TOST) for the main learned-vs-best-classical comparisons S1-S8

Difference = learned minus best equal-tooled classical (success-rate settings in pp; tracking settings S1-S2 in % of the classical RMSE, sign chosen so that positive = learned better in every row). Two-one-sided-test logic via the 90% paired-bootstrap CI: 'equivalent' if the whole 90% CI lies inside the margin. The margin is the project's own +-10 pp (S1-S2: +-10% of classical RMSE, sign flipped so that positive = learned better, the pre-specified tracking threshold); a +-5 pp column is added because r1 (M8) asked for two margins. Bootstrap CI at small n is only approximate (inference).

Verdict key: EQUIV = whole 90% CI inside the margin (equivalence shown at that margin); 'L worse' / 'L better' = whole 90% CI beyond -margin / +margin; 'no' = CI crosses a margin, so neither equivalence nor a clear difference can be claimed (the honest wording is 'no detectable difference at the +10 pp bar' only when the 95% CI also excludes +10 on the learned-better side).

Notes. (1) The learned side is the per-episode mean over training seeds, as in the original tables; this makes CIs narrower than for a single run (s10b table caveat b). (2) For S1-S2 the tracking margin is relative (10% of classical RMSE) because pp does not apply; sign flipped so positive = learned better (lower RMSE). (3) 'best learned' per setting is the highest-mean variant listed, i.e. chosen post hoc, which favours the learned side; the all-variants listing is shown for S5-S7. (4) Equivalence of a learner that did not learn only says it is near its initialisation (the classical base); it is not evidence that learning is useless.

## 3. Summary for the paper text (round 2)

Rows of record (the legacy rows are excluded from the lists below):
- EQUIV at +-10 (90% CI inside): S2-N1-dist, S3-bc, S3-mip, S3-diffusion, S3-flow10, S3-flow1 (relative RMSE margin), S4-restitution (pilot), S5-oracle (legacy), S7-L-est-full, S7-L-est-eff, S7-PPO (13a), S7-OOD
- EQUIV also at +-5: S2-N1-dist, S3-bc, S3-mip, S3-flow10, S3-flow1, S5-oracle (legacy), S7-L-est-full, S7-PPO (13a)
- No equivalence claim possible (CI crosses a margin): S1-W0-clean, S1-W0-dist, S1-W3-clean, S1-W3-dist, S6-oracle (legacy), S8-canon
- Learned clearly worse than classical beyond the -10 margin: S2-N1-clean, S4-mass, S4-sensing, S5-SAC (legacy), S5-PPO (15b), S6-L-est, S6-PPO (15b), S8-multi
- Learned clearly better beyond the margin: none
- Reading of the new rows (inference): S5/S6 PPO under the single-seed-gate exploration scale are not "equivalent" but clearly worse (-23.8 and -17.6 pp), so the old legacy EQUIV/no-decision labels for S5-PPO/S6-PPO must not be quoted. S7-PPO (13a) is EQUIV, but it is "not learned", so equivalence there only says the residual stayed near zero. S3 students are equivalent to the teacher within +-10% RMSE (diffusion 6.2% worse, so it is "L worse" at +-5%), and the setting has no headroom.
